State vs Prashant Gaur on 15 February, 2024
Sc No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors
 In The Court Of Sh. Gautam Manan, Asj-05
 East, Karkardoomama, Delhi

15.02.2024
 Order On Charge
 1.
By present order I will decide the question of framing of charge against the accused persons in case titled as "State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors " FIR No. 476/20, PS Shakapur.

2. Brief facts of the case are that complainant Deepali lodged a complaint before CAW Cell against her husband Prashant Gaur (since deceased) and her in-laws Dinesh Gaur, Usha Devi (parents-in-law), Sachin (brother- in-law) and Aashu (sister-in-law) for committing physical and mental cruelty, for demand of dowry, unnatural sex, criminal breach of trust, miscarriage by using force and for causing hurt to her.

3. Complaint resulted into a FIR in question and accused persons husband Prashant Gaur (since deceased) and her in-laws Dinesh Gaur, Usha Devi (parents-in-law) and Sachin (brother-in-law)
were charge-sheeted for offence punishable under Section 498A/406/357/313/377/34 IPC.
SC No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors 4.

entities.text: SC No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On behalf of the State and complainant it is submitted that as per the allegations accused persons committed cruelty against complainant and she was subjected to forcible abortion by her husband and mother- in-law Usha Devi.

It is stated that the allegations are specific that mental and physical cruelty was inflicted by accused persons upon the complainant on account of demand of dowry and hence, charge be framed against all accused persons.

5. It is submitted on behalf of accused persons that allegations against accused persons are general in nature and there is no material on record which indicates that due to demand of dowry, any cruelty was committed by the accused persons.
It is further submitted that there is no material on record to frame the charge for offence punishable under section 313 IPC as well.

In support of its contentions, Ld. Counsel for accused persons has relied upon case titled as 'Union of India Vs.
Praffula Kumar Samal & Anr. ' (1979) 3 SCC 4 and Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors."

I have heard rival contentions and have gone through record.
SC No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors Allegations under Section 313 IPC 7.

sentences.text:
Section 313 IPC reads as under:
313. Causing miscarriage without woman's consent:
Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
8.

In this respect, complainant in her initial complaint dated 20.07.2020 stated as under:
" ......

In the month of August 2017, I again got pregnant but no one cares for me and this time again my husband along with my mother in law took me for abortion of my pregnancy to the Nanda Hospital, sec-15. Faridabad, where my pregnancy was again aborted without my consent.

After abortion I was feeling very weak and sick but even then my husband, mother-in-law, father- in-law forced me to done the entire household works and after doing so I got ill but they did not provide me any treatment.

9. It is matter of record that statement of complainant was also got recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C, and her allegations with regard to forcible abortion reads as under:
SC No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors ....

entities.text: SC No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In June 2017, I again conceived and my mother-in-law and my husband forcibly got my abortion on 17 August 2017 at Nanda Hospital, Sector- 15,Faridabad.....

10. Though complainant alleged that her husband (since deceased) and her mother-in-law Usha Devi forcibly got her abortion done but it is matter of record that complainant did not take any action against the accused persons for committing such an act.
For the first time in her complaint dated 20.07.2020 which was made after 3 years of incident the complainant come up with this allegation.
11. None the less, the allegations in respect of forcible abortion is contrary to medical record collected by the investigating agency.
Medical record obtained by Investigating agency where the abortion took place that complainant duly consented for it.

She has signed on the consent form which mention that she understood the necessity and the nature of the operation, consequences,
risks, complication and procedure of the operation.

2 12.
Medical record further indicates that there was no cardiac activity for which the abortion procedure was undertaken.
Therefore, there is no material on record which even prima-facie shows that complainant was forced to abort the child by the accused persons.

Prashant Gaur & Ors 13

. In Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors Vs State of Bihar & Ors 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 141 Hon'ble Apex Court observed as under:
17.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors Vs State of Bihar & Ors 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 141
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Recently, in K. Subba Rao v. The State of Telangana, it was also observed that:
"6. The Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: K. Subba Rao v. The State of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out."
18.

The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of Section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes, without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute,
if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.

14. In the case of Sajjan Kumar vs. CBI (2010) 9 SCC 368 , Hon'ble Apex Court on consideration of the various decisions about the scope of Sections 227 and 228 of the Code, laid down the following principles:
(i) The Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under Section 227 of the Cr.P.C. has the undoubted power to sift and SC No. 334/23 State Vs.
Prashant Gaur & Ors weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.
The test to determine prima facie case would depend upon the facts of each case.

ii) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained, the Court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.

iii) The Court cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouthpiece of the prosecution but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities, etc.
However, at this stage, there cannot be a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial.

State vs Prashant Gaur on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47769628/
3

iv) If on the basis of the material on record, the Court could form an opinion that the accused might have committed offence, it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has committed the offence.

v) At the time of framing of the charges, the probative value of the material on record cannot be gone into but before framing a charge the Court must apply its judicial mind on the material placed on record and must be satisfied that the commission of offence by the accused was possible.

vi) At the stage of Sections227 and 228, the Court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to find out if the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value discloses the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.

For this limited purpose, sift the evidence as it cannot be expected SC No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors even at that initial stage to accept all that the prosecution states as gospel truth even if it is opposed to common sense or the broad probabilities of the case.

entities.text: SC No. 334/23 State Vs. Prashant Gaur & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: vii) If two views are possible and one of them gives rise to suspicion only, as distinguished from grave suspicion, the trial Judge will be empowered to discharge the accused and at this stage, he is not to see whether the trial will end in conviction or acquittal.
15. It is evident that there is no material on record which gives rise to grave suspicion against accused persons to have committed the offence of forcible abortion.

Considering the principles as laid down in above stated authoritative pronouncement, it has to be concluded that charge for the offence punishable under Section 313/34 IPC is not made out against accused persons.

16. Accordingly, accused Usha Devi against whom allegations of forcible abortion were made is discharged for the offence punishable under Section 313/34 IPC.
17.

As the accused persons are charge-sheeted for other offences which are triable by the Court of Magistrate, matter be sent to the Court of Ld. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, East, Karkardooma to mark the case to jurisdictional Magistrate's Court to proceed further with the case of prosecution for the other offences for which accused persons are charge-sheeted in accordance with law.
